subject: Vertera trial blueprint, success criteria & ownership
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@vertera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vertera trial blueprint, success criteria & ownership

Alex — thanks again for a productive conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the trial moving this week. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Call recap (30 min):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference reduces per-request latency and cost for Vertera's document ingestion chatflow while preserving answer accuracy for top-10 query intents.
- Primary success metrics agreed: median latency < 250ms (p50), 99th percentile latency < 700ms under your expected concurrency (50 reqs/min), and top-10 intent accuracy >= 92% (measured by your evaluation set).
- Scope: 2-week POC against a 10k-doc test corpus + representative prompt set (we'll use a redacted slice of your production corpus).
- Owners: Vertera product lead (Alex) to provide sample corpus, Redwood (Logan) to deliver environment and initial SOW, and Redwood CS (Marissa) to run weekly measurement and checkpoints.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Day 0–2: access & infra — Vertera provides S3 read-only test bucket + service account; Redwood provision private POC instance (dedicated capacity) and share endpoints.
2) Day 3–5: baseline run — run your prompt set on current infra; collect latency/cost baselines.
3) Day 6–10: tuning & validation — apply batching/quantization profile and run A/B vs baseline; gather accuracy results.
4) Day 11–14: final report & handoff — deliver report, runbook, and recommendations.

Attachments: Vertera_Success-Criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet with metric definitions) and POC-SOW-v1.pdf (draft scope + statement of work).

Open asks for Vertera:
- Provide sample corpus (S3 path) and a service account for read access by Wed 6/16 EOD.
- Confirm your quality lead who will review evaluation outputs (name + contact).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Marissa will schedule the kickoff runbook session once we receive access.
- Ben will scope reserved capacity and confirm instance sizing by Wed 6/16.

Proposed time for kickoff: Thu 6/17 10:00–10:45 PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — aiming to keep this tight so you have a clear pass/fail after two weeks.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
redwood.ai
From: Alex Morgan <alex@vertera.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@vertera.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vertera trial blueprint, success criteria & ownership

Thanks Logan — summary looks right to me. Quick answers below.

- Sample corpus: I shared an S3 path (s3://vertera-poc/samples/2027-06) with read-only IAM role access for redwood-poc@vertera-service. Let me know if you need a different principal.
- Quality lead: Priya Shah (cc’d) will own accuracy reviews and sign-off on the top-10 intents.
- Kickoff: Thu 6/17 10:00 PT works on our side.

Two clarifications:
1) We have a separate redaction step in our pipeline — for the POC we can provide already-redacted documents, but if Redwood needs to validate redaction behavior let us know and we can provide rules.
2) On metric windows: can you confirm whether latency targets are measured end-to-end (client->client) or just the inference step? We prefer end-to-end but can accept inference-only for comparability.

I reviewed the SOW briefly — looks fine. We’ll expect a final SOW before provisioning reserved capacity.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform, Vertera
alex@vertera.com | +1 212-555-0345

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vertera trial blueprint, success criteria & ownership

Looping in a couple notes from infra sizing and CS readiness:

- Capacity: I ran a quick estimate given the 50 reqs/min concurrency target and the document sizes you described. We recommend a single p4d-equivalent reserved slice with burst headroom — should keep p50 well under your 250ms target with the batching profile we intend to try. I’ll provide the exact SKU + monthly cost in a follow-up by EOD Mon 6/21.
- Credentials: thanks for the S3 path, Alex. We still need the IAM principal (email) that will be allowed to assume access. If you can add redwood-svc@redwood-poc (or confirm the principal you already granted) that’ll unblock Day 0.
- Eval harness: Marissa — can you confirm you’re able to run the provided evaluation notebook against Vertera’s dataset? I put a starter checklist in the drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Vertera-POC

Also want to call out a small data hygiene ask: in the sample corpus we saw ~3% of documents with malformed JSON metadata; if we can get a cleaned slice (or a quick mapping for those records) that’ll reduce noise in accuracy measurements.

I’ll align on SKU + cost and share an updated POC-SOW-v1 with a short addendum for burst and logging retention.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Alex / Priya — quick weekly nudge as we head into the POC kickoff window. Status & next actions below.

Status:
- Access: Alex confirmed S3 path; Ben flagged we still need the IAM principal to be added for redwood-svc@redwood-poc (ask from infra).
- SOW: Ben is updating the SOW with SKU and burst addendum; Marissa will upload the kickoff runbook once the principal is confirmed.
- Data: noticed Ben’s note about malformed JSON in ~3% of docs — if Vertera can provide a cleaned slice or a mapping by Tue 6/29 that would be ideal.

Immediate asks (can you please):
1) Confirm IAM principal for S3 access (add redwood-svc@redwood-poc) — today/Tue 6/29.
2) Priya — confirm the accuracy review rubric contact and preferred reporting cadence (daily diff CSVs or an end-of-day summarized spreadsheet).
3) Alex — confirm kickoff time (Thu 6/17 invite was proposed earlier; if that still works we’ll lock calendar).

If we don’t have the principal by EOD Wed 6/30, we’ll still stand up the environment but request running the baseline with a smaller dev sample to avoid blocking the timeline.

Thanks — short call if you prefer, otherwise we’ll track here.

—
